solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Picture of Carol at home, repeatedly plugged by the artist

parts.note: to carol is to sing

indicators.note: plugged by says something is stopped up by another piece pushed into it

parts.note: at home means IN, here taken three times over
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone sings carols at home while an artist keeps interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' here means three times over, not twice; RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist. The song title drops the g: Singin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and this is the famous 1952 Gene Kelly musical.

clue.text: Our lot, blue at the extremities, are freezing!

definitions.note: a verbal noun standing for the verb: to freeze payments is to put them on hold

indicators.note: at the extremities puts the word for blue on either side of the other piece

parts.note: to blue money is to blow or spend it
our lot means us

explanation.surface: A cold group of people turning blue at their fingers and toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is a verb, to squander money, not a colour; 'at the extremities' wraps it round US.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze an account or payment is to halt it temporarily.

clue.text: Little tree giving up nothing? One silver nutmeg, at first

indicators.note: in a down answer, giving up sends the built string upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
one is the Roman numeral I
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A footballer asks whether a small sapling gives nothing away, offering one silver nutmeg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving up' reverses O, I, AG and N in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a small New Zealand tree or shrub.

clue.text: Engine horn is or should be blown with energy

indicators.note: blown means wrecked or scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A car's horn ought to be sounded vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Should be blown' rearranges HORNISOR into IRONHORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old nickname for a railway locomotive.

clue.text: African heart-throb — girls must turn up to show!

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reads the letters from bottom to top
to show says the letters are on display within the words

explanation.surface: A dashing idol insists girls attend his appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To show' finds OBGI spanning the words, and 'must turn up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Igbo are a people of south-eastern Nigeria, so a member is an African.

clue.text: Are demanding to be given new offshore location?

parts.note: to tax is to make demands on, so the word for demanding gives TAX
to have is to be given or receive

explanation.surface: People insisting on being handed something fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' just links the pieces; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Many low-tax jurisdictions sit on islands away from the mainland, hence offshore banking.

clue.text: Cross into western half of Europe, second-rate out-of-town area

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other
western half takes the first, left-hand, half of the word

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
B is second class, as in B-grade

explanation.surface: Travelling into western Europe ends in a shabby place outside a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Europe has six letters, so its western half is EUR; X goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An exurb is a district beyond the suburbs, outside a city.

clue.text: Pair filmed briefly moving part of roadie's kit?

indicators.note: moving signals the letters shift into a new order
briefly cuts the last letter from the word

explanation.surface: Two people were filmed carrying a roadie's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' clips FILMED to FILME; 'moving' rearranges PAIRFILME.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadies set up a band's sound gear, of which the amp is one example.

clue.text: In northern lands, 16 grand found in raw gold

indicators.note: In puts the following pieces inside the outer ones

parts.note: to land a prize is to get it
the answer to 16 Down is universal, and U is the film certificate for universal
G is a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Prospectors in the north find a thousand pounds' worth of raw gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 Down is UNIVERSAL, a British film rating abbreviated U.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuggets are lumps of unrefined gold as they are found.

clue.text: Doctor who's bad with old x-ray: do ring practice!

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: X-ray is X in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A doctor whose old X-ray is poor tells someone to train for boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor who' looks like the TV show; 'Doctor' rearranges WHOSBAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadowbox is to spar with no opponent, as training for the boxing ring.

clue.text: University no place for one free of attachment

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to free from being fastened

parts.note: N abbreviates no, as on a yes/no form
a peg is a place for one thing, such as a coat to hang

explanation.surface: A university is no place for someone without ties.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg something is to unfasten it by removing its pins.

clue.text: The Times: can it manage reverses?

indicators.note: reverses turns the built word backwards

parts.note: can it means be quiet, which is SH
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Asks whether The Times newspaper can survive setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' is not the newspaper but periods of history; 'reverses' turns SHCOPE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochs are eras or ages, the times of history.

clue.text: Fresh trouble and strife occasioned by the same?

definitions.text: Fresh trouble and strife occasioned by the same?

indicators.note: occasioned by puts the cause first in the answer

parts.note: the same means strife, which here is war
trouble and strife is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, so a fresh one is a bride

explanation.surface: A new wife brings fresh trouble from the same quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' is Cockney rhyming slang for wife; 'the same' points back to strife, here war.
explanation.definitionFit: A war bride is a woman married during wartime, often to a serviceman from abroad.

clue.text: What's just sweet to the ear?

indicators.note: to the ear says the word is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a sweet is a dessert, a pudding

explanation.surface: Asking what pudding tastes like when you only hear about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is a noun, the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: One's deserts are what one deserves, as in just deserts.

clue.text: Has torn about in a rage, prematurely ending state of bliss?

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled letters around the other piece
torn means ripped up, so the letters are scrambled
prematurely ending cuts the word short by its last letter

parts.note: in a rage means angrily

explanation.surface: Someone has stormed about furiously, cutting short a happy state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn' turns HAS into SHA, which goes 'about' ANGRIL, ANGRILY 'prematurely ending'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La, the hidden valley in Hilton's Lost Horizon, stands for an earthly paradise.

clue.text: Mount very retrograde operation against one from America

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: use means operation, as in in use
V is versus, against
one is I in Roman numerals
US means from America

explanation.surface: A very backward operation set against an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrograde' reverses USE to ESU.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesuvius is the volcano overlooking Naples, so a mountain.

clue.text: Bath, say, girl left clutching small blanket

parts.note: Bath has a university, a UNI, by example

indicators.note: clutching holds the small piece inside

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl at Bath leaves holding a small blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city with a university; 'Bath, say' looks like a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket ban is all-embracing, applying to everyone.

clue.text: Russian writer, having invited press in, opening up

indicators.note: having invited puts the guest piece within the host
in confirms that one piece sits inside the other
in a down answer up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: a vent is an opening
to press is to urge

explanation.surface: A Russian author invites journalists in and opens up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists but is the verb, to urge; 'up' reads the opening backwards, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev wrote Fathers and Sons, a classic of 19th-century Russian fiction.

clue.text: Guilty of a fumble, tripping close to ball

indicators.note: tripping means stumbling, a sign the letters fall into new order
close to takes the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fielder fumbling near the ball is at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' rearranges AFUMBLE to BLAMEFU; 'close to' takes L from ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameful means deserving reproach, at fault.

clue.text: Rumour saying one might go through deal

parts.note: a buzz is a rumour going round
a saw is a proverb or saying

explanation.surface: A rumour that a saying might get through a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is the timber of pine or fir, not a business agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered circular saw cuts timber, including the softwood called deal.

clue.text: From dark heap picked up a sort of acid

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: night means dark, and a rick is a heap of hay

explanation.surface: A sample of acid taken from a shadowy pile.
explanation.walkthrough: A rick is a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid, HNO3, is a strong corrosive acid.

clue.text: Thus crew initially without a steer?

definitions.text: Thus crew initially without a steer?

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
less means without

explanation.surface: A rowing crew with no one to steer the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' is the animal, an ox, in the wordplay and steering in the whole reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxless boat is rowed with no coxswain steering, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Boy's engaging ME strip, casting article in Serpentine

indicators.note: engaging means holding within

parts.note: Ziggy is a boy's name, and the 's means has

indicators.note: casting means throwing into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged once the article is cast out

parts.note: the Gaza Strip is in the Middle East, ME
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boy dons a strip, losing an article in the Serpentine lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' rearranges GAZA less A into ZAG, which ZIGGY engages. The Serpentine is a lake in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine means winding like a snake, so a zigzag course.

clue.text: In one area old country has abandoned pit

indicators.note: has abandoned takes the named letters away

parts.note: Abyssinia is the old name of Ethiopia
taken as written
one is I

explanation.surface: An old nation has given up a pit in a region.
explanation.walkthrough: ABYSSINIA abandons INIA, the IN, I and A spelt at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm or bottomless pit.

clue.text: Old kingdom is under obligation to drop first one, then the other

indicators.note: to drop the first one removes the opening letter

parts.note: someone under obligation owes
the other is a coy British euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: An old realm must shed one thing and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of the other' is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the West Saxons.

clue.text: Out of the mouth appeared a tongue

indicators.note: out of the mouth means spoken, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: appeared means shown, followed by A

explanation.surface: A tongue appeared out of someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' is a language, not the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Shona is a Bantu language spoken in Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Lump of skin: hurry to conceal odd bits

indicators.note: to conceal odd bits hides the odd-numbered letters, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A skin lump: hurry to cover the odd parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lump of skin' looks like the definition; only 'Lump' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A knur is a knot or hard swelling, as in a tree trunk.

clue.text: Pointed to spot, clutching hip

indicators.note: clutching holds the other piece inside

parts.note: to spy is to spot
in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Someone pointed to a spot while holding their hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' is an adjective, sharp, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny means covered in sharp points, like a cactus.

clue.text: Pole with heart ringing Spanish girl's number

indicators.note: ringing surrounds the other piece

parts.note: N is the north pole
a core is a heart
Ines is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A Pole with feeling phones a Spanish girl's number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a Polish person but a pole of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine score is nine times twenty, 180.

clue.text: Have more than one bowler as an all-rounder?

definitions.text: Have more than one bowler as an all-rounder?

parts.words: Have more than one bowler as an all-rounder?
parts.note: a bowler is a hard felt hat as well as a cricketer who bowls, and an all-rounder in cricket fills both batting and bowling roles

explanation.walkthrough: A bowler is a cricket bowler and a hat; an all-rounder plays both batting and bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear several hats is an idiom for holding several roles at once.
